briefings.title: AlphaGenome author roundtable
briefings.tldr: AlphaGenome is Google DeepMind's new AI model, published in "Nature," that unifies DNA sequence-to-function prediction, representing a significant step towards deciphering the entire genome.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AlphaGenome is Google DeepMind's new AI model, published in "Nature," that unifies DNA sequence-to-function prediction, representing a significant step towards deciphering the entire genome. It leverages novel architectural and data handling techniques to predict the functional impact of genetic variants across the vast non-coding regions, addressing critical unmet needs in understanding genetic diseases and fundamental biology.

## AlphaGenome's Mission and Impact
*   **Deciphering the Genome Source Code:** The team's overarching mission is to build an AI system to decipher the genome sequence, the "source code of life," with enormous potential benefits for health and other areas.
    *   Measuring progress involves assessing how well the system predicts the effects of mutations (small DNA changes) on cellular molecular mechanisms.
*   **Addressing Undiagnosed Genetic Diseases:** Improving genome understanding is crucial, as a "large fraction of rare genetic diseases remain undiagnosed today" due to poor genomic comprehension.
    *   AI is positioned as an "impactful application" for reading the genome and making meaningful predictions about genetic mutations.
*   **Expanding Genomic Coverage:** AlphaGenome significantly extends previous work (e.g., AlphaMissense, which covered only the 2% coding region) to focus on the **non-coding 98% of the genome**, illuminating its majority.

## Technical Breakthroughs and Unique Capabilities
*   **Unified Multi-Modal Prediction:** AlphaGenome uniquely models more modalities (molecular mechanisms) in one model than ever before, combining long input sequence length and finely detailed predictions.
    *   It inputs **megabases of DNA sequence** and outputs predictions at **single-base resolution** for many output types.
    *   This fills a gap left by previous models that either specialized (e.g., SpliceAI, Orca) or traded off resolution for context length (e.g., Informer, Borzoi).
*   **Overcoming Computational Hurdles:** The model addresses prior computational limits and high-memory usage associated with long-range, high-resolution, multi-modal predictions.
    *   **Distributed sequence processing:** Spliced sequences into shorter subsequences processed by multiple TPUs that communicate to maintain context, inspired by a breakthrough lunch discussion.
    *   **Optimized data loading:** Managed vast training data (up to 50 GB) by compressing sparse modalities (99% zeros) and rigorously quality-checking data for high quality and diversity.
*   **Integration of Complex Biological Modalities:** AlphaGenome successfully integrates predictions for diverse biological processes.
    *   **Splicing:** Models the process of bringing non-contiguous genetic information together for protein expression, a capability new to the team and the field, handling 2D sparse array predictions.
    *   **Contact Maps:** Captures 2D interactions between DNA regions vital for gene regulation (e.g., promoter-enhancer interactions) without degrading performance on other modalities.

## Comprehensive Evaluation and API Release
*   **Rigorous Two-Pronged Evaluation Strategy:** Model performance was assessed on both new DNA sequences and, critically, on variant effect prediction.
    *   **Variant effect prediction:** Compares predictions from reference vs. mutated DNA sequences to identify and summarize differences, overcoming initial challenges with **11 gigabyte outputs** via a new, fast variant scoring API.
    *   **Parallelized evaluation:** The team parallelized evaluation efforts, with individuals owning specific modalities or areas, often using pre-existing community benchmarks.
    *   **Multi-level evaluation:** Evaluations covered molecular-level recapitulation of experimental data and organism-level consequences like disease risk, including a surprising success in predicting cancer driver mutations.
*   **Accessible API for the Community:** AlphaGenome was released with a user-friendly API simultaneously with its preprint, allowing immediate interaction without specialized hardware (e.g., GPUs) or complex setup.
    *   Users can quickly make predictions and visualize results in a notebook environment.
    *   The team directly manages user support via a Discourse forum, actively soliciting feedback on case studies, gaps, and ideas.
*   **Efficient Development:** The entire process from initial prototype discussion to paper publication was completed in **under two years** through intensive team collaboration.

## Future Directions and Impact
*   **Enhanced User Experience and Summarization:** Plans include aggregating the tens of thousands of scores per variant into more digestible single scores, aiding scientists in prioritizing variants for deeper analysis.
*   **Enabling Large-Scale Genomic Analysis:** The team aims to pre-compute as many variants as possible to support large-scale analyses, such as genome-wide association studies, which require extensive predictions.
*   **Open-Sourcing Model Weights:** Releasing the model weights will empower researchers to experiment with embeddings, fine-tune the model, or extend it with new data, fostering diverse, unforeseen applications.
*   **Expanding Capabilities with Single-Cell Data:** Future improvements include leveraging new single-cell atlases to extend the model's applicability to individual cell types within tissues, enhancing its relevance for disease studies.
*   **Broadening Scientific Utility:** AlphaGenome is poised to be a foundational tool for pinpointing harmful mutations, understanding basic biology (e.g., functional genome parts, gene regulation, cell type activation), and maximizing research efficiency and funding returns.

## Notable Quotes
> "The mission of the team is to build an AI system that will allow us to decipher the genome sequence... Deciphering this source code would have enormous benefit in health and many other areas." - Ziga on the team's mission

> "The gap that AlphaGenome has filled is that it's modeling more modalities in one model than ever before. The input sequence length is very long, and the predictions are very finely detailed. It's a powerful combination of these three things." - on AlphaGenome's unique contribution

> "With AlphaGenome, scientists can hopefully use it to maximize the return on their limited resources and funding, thereby improving scientific research." - Jun on the practical utility for scientists

> "If we could extend the model with these [new single-cell atlases], it would be more applicable to studying variants associated with diseases where, for example, this defect arises in these individual cell types." - Ziga on future capabilities and impact

briefings.title: Bill Winters - CEO of Standard Chartered  Podcast  In Good Company
briefings.tldr: Standard Chartered CEO Bill Winters reflects on a decade leading the bank, having navigated a profound crisis involving compliance and credit issues to establish a robust "connector bank" model.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Standard Chartered CEO Bill Winters reflects on a decade leading the bank, having navigated a profound crisis involving compliance and credit issues to establish a robust "connector bank" model. The bank, with its deep roots in Asia, Africa, and the Middle East, is now strategically positioned to leverage digital asset transformation, adapt to global geopolitical shifts, and foster a culture of curiosity and calculated risk-taking.

## Standard Chartered: A Unique Global Connector
*   **Deep historical roots inform its global identity:**
    *   Founded in 1853, combining the Standard Bank of Africa and the Chartered Bank of India, China, and Australia.
    *   Originated to finance trade within the British Empire, a core activity that remains central today.
*   **Operates as a "connector bank," not just an emerging markets player:**
    *   Maintains physical operations in **55 markets** and coverage in another **120 via fly-in/fly-out**.
    *   Has significant operations in the US and Europe, noting that markets like Hong Kong and Singapore are no longer "emerging."
    *   Serves as the **second-largest trade bank in Asia**, the world's biggest trading hub.
    *   **Focuses on connecting markets and people** by leveraging multiple "home" markets globally.
        *   **UK:** Serves as the headquarters and primary regulatory home.
        *   **Hong Kong/China:** Constitutes the biggest single market and largest profit source.
        *   **Singapore:** Functions as a major operational hub.
        *   **India:** Acts as a significant operation center and a large banking presence.
*   **Clientele primarily consists of multinational entities:**
    *   Roughly **two-thirds** of the business comes from corporate and institutional clients, including governments, almost all of whom are multinational and require cross-border nexus.
    *   **One-third** is retail, exclusively in Asia, the Middle East, and Africa.
    *   Provides financing for local operations and connects clients to local supply chain players, distributors, and partners.
*   **Strategic rationale for maintaining London headquarters:**
    *   **Sophisticated regulatory environment:** The UK regulators, particularly the Bank of England, are highly experienced in managing complex global banks, especially those active in financial markets and derivatives.
    *   **Premier financial center:** London provides essential financial infrastructure and a favorable time zone for operations across Africa, Western Europe, and the Americas.
    *   **Neutrality:** Headquartering in London helps avoid having to choose between key hubs like Hong Kong (where SC's name is on banknotes) and Singapore (where Temasek is its largest shareholder).

## The Decade of Turnaround: Strategy & Execution (2014-Present)
*   **Inherited a bank in deep crisis (2014):**
    *   Upon his arrival, Standard Chartered faced substantial **compliance problems** (predominantly with the US, but also UK and others) and significant **credit problems**.
    *   The bank's share price had fallen by **75% from its peak**, having previously been lauded as a "darling of the City."
    *   Required writing off **a quarter of the bank's book equity** and necessitated a rights offering to recapitalize.
*   **Prioritizing regulatory confidence and strategic team building:**
    *   Winters had a crucial **three-month observation period** before starting, allowing for deep due diligence without immediate decision-making pressure.
    *   **Established regulators as the "single number one priority,"** essential for regaining trust and maintaining operating licenses (e.g., US dollar clearing), even if initially "at the expense of shareholders."
    *   Built a core executive team by promoting approximately half from within and hiring the other half externally (e.g., Chief Risk Officer, Head of Corporate Bank).
    *   **Emphasized integrity and team focus**, addressing prior instances of "self-serving behavior" and "control lapses."
*   **Challenges and the path to recovery:**
    *   **Acknowledged an initial overcorrection:** Hit the brakes too hard on risk appetite, resulting in an unnecessary shrinkage of the balance sheet by roughly **one-third** in the first year.
    *   **Addressed a significant technology deficit**, closing gaps in systems and obsolescence.
    *   Felt internal improvements were substantial by **2019**, despite missing public targets due to unforeseen interest rate drops.
    *   Market recognition for the turnaround lagged internal sentiment, only becoming evident in **2022-2023** due to factors like the COVID-19 pandemic, a historical "credibility gap," and the bank's relatively smaller size compared to peers like HSBC.
    *   Drew on prior experience fixing JP Morgan Chase after the 2001 crises, understanding that tough situations can yield positive long-term outcomes for shareholders.

## Adapting to a New Global Order
*   **Navigating intensifying geopolitical tensions:**
    *   Acknowledges a "super tense" global environment, with daily concerns about developments in major regions.
    *   **Believes in fundamental self-interest of major powers:** Assumes the US and China will avoid self-harm despite intense, persistent competition, which he expects to last "my entire lifetime and beyond."
    *   Observes that, broadly, the world is currently experiencing "less major conflict than right now" historically, despite localized crises.
*   **Advocates for "resetting globalization":**
    *   Aims to preserve the wealth and prosperity generated by globalization while consciously addressing populations and regions "left behind" by de-industrialization.
    *   Includes a renewed focus on human rights, indigenous peoples, and environmental sustainability (e.g., managing greenhouse gas emissions), areas neglected in previous globalization waves.
*   **Foresees emerging multi-polar financial systems:**
    *   Fears a gradual move towards separate financial infrastructures, with China actively building alternatives to the dollar-centric Bretton Woods system.
    *   China's objective is to ensure continued trading access even if dollar access is restricted, rather than to displace the dollar as a reserve or trade currency.
    *   **Standard Chartered actively operates in both emerging financial systems**, acting as a crucial "bridge."
    *   Notes that key countries like India, Brazil, South Africa, and those in the Middle East are unlikely to choose sides, which will help maintain interoperability.
*   **Key regional outlooks:**
    *   **China:** Long-term optimism due to technical and technological advantages, despite currently navigating an "ugly" property bubble deflation and equity market challenges. Current **4.8% GDP growth** is below its potential as a middle-income country, and a full recovery could take **3-4 more years**.
    *   **India:** Hailed as a "powerhouse," benefiting significantly from Prime Minister Modi's **10-year reforms**, evidenced by recent **8% GDP growth**. Recognizes more structural reforms and infrastructure development are needed.
    *   **Middle East:** Transforming from an oil and creditor economy to a developing, diversified, and capital-consumptive region. Dubai, in particular, is attracting significant wealth (mostly Indian/South Asian) and parts of the asset management industry.

## The Future of Banking: Digital Assets, AI, & Culture
*   **Digital assets poised to revolutionize banking:**
    *   **Core conviction: "Eventually all things will settle on blockchains,"** including securities, money/payments, and real-world assets (property, art, etc.).
    *   **Benefits:** Blockchain-based settlement is cheaper, easier, more transparent, traceable, and real-time.
    *   **Main obstacles:** Primarily regulatory concerns, stemming from the association of blockchain with criminal cryptocurrency activities and the potential for stablecoins to drain deposits from traditional banking systems.
    *   Standard Chartered has invested in this area for **seven years**, developing leading institutional-grade platforms for stablecoin-based payments and tokenized bank deposits.
*   **AI as a transformative force:**
    *   **Current impact:** Already significantly improving fraud detection, anti-money laundering, and compliance, drastically enhancing the ability to fight financial crime (though only **3% of global financial crime** is currently captured).
    *   **Productivity gains:** Being used for code generation in large-scale systems development.
    *   **Future applications:** Expected to drive major changes in product development, customer service (through scaled deployment of AI agents), and personalized advice.
*   **Corporate culture: Emphasizing collaboration and tackling complexity:**
    *   **Defining characteristic:** A highly collaborative culture, rooted in the bank's structural diversity across its **55 physical markets**.
    *   **Areas for improvement:** Addressing the inherent "slowness of decision-making and getting things done," partly due to lingering risk aversion and the complexities of a diverse organization.
    *   **Strategy for change:** Implementing "hardware" (streamlining processes mechanically) and "software" (improving feedback systems to recognize execution and collaboration).
    *   **Obsession with speed:** Aims to accelerate decision-making, believing faster decisions are generally better, and measures process turnaround times (e.g., onboarding from **60 days to 6 hours**).
*   **Leadership philosophy on risk, learning, and personal example:**
    *   **Tolerant of "errors of judgment"** but **"completely intolerant of errors of principle"** (which result in instant exit).
    *   Encourages calculated risk-taking and learning from non-successes; its Venture Lab, for example, has commercialized **40 out of 2,300 considered investments**.
    *   While not seeking to be the sole role model, Winters champions a collective leadership that demonstrates **curiosity and empathy**, which he sees as "the two defining terms for leadership."
    *   **Personal drivers:** Driven by intense curiosity, a love for learning (geopolitics, innovation), and empathy; views ambition as a "curse" that can lead to perpetual dissatisfaction.
    *   **Advice to young people:** "Take a risk" and "go the reckless route" early in their careers when recovery from setbacks is easier, reflecting his own career-defining "reckless" decisions.

## Notable Quotes
> "People sometimes refer to us as an emerging markets bank, but that is not quite right... Really, we are a connector bank. We just connect markets to markets and people to people because we have multiple home markets." - Bill Winters on **Standard Chartered's identity**

> "The very first and most important communicators were with regulators because the bank had lost their confidence. So, my first interactions were to be very clear that the regulators were the single number one priority, even at the expense of shareholders... because that was necessary for existence at that point." - Bill Winters on **prioritizing regulatory trust during the turnaround**

> "Our view, which was probably quite controversial a few years ago but less so today, is that eventually all things will settle on blockchains. 'All things' certainly means securities, but also money, so payments, and then eventually real-world assets like property, art, wine, or whatever else people might want to invest in." - Bill Winters on **the future of digital assets in banking**

> "When you get to a fork in the road, take it... when you do come to a turning point from time to time, go the reckless route. And if you go the reckless route early, you can recover very easily." - Bill Winters on **career advice for young people**

briefings.title: Davos 2026 IMFs Kristalina Georgieva on whats next for AI skills and the global economy
briefings.tldr: The global economy shows surprising resilience with upgraded growth projections despite pervasive uncertainty, driven by private sector dynamism and muted trade tensions.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
The global economy shows surprising resilience with upgraded growth projections despite pervasive uncertainty, driven by private sector dynamism and muted trade tensions. Artificial intelligence is a powerful driver of future growth but necessitates thoughtful policy to manage its transformative impact on jobs, mitigate risks, and ensure inclusive prosperity.

## The New Normal of Uncertainty & Global Economic Resilience
*   **Uncertainty is the new normal:** The world is now genuinely multi-polar, driven by rapid technological shifts, climate change, and diverse demographic trends (aging vs. youthful populations).
    *   Leaders must "learn to think of the unthinkable and then stay calm" to adapt.
*   **Global Economy Shows Surprising Resilience:** The IMF has upgraded global growth projections to **3.3%** for this year and **3.2%** for next, returning to pre-tariff tension levels.
    *   **Four key factors contributing to this resilience:**
        *   **Dynamic Private Sector:** Governments have stepped back from running companies, allowing the more adaptable and agile private sector to drive growth.
        *   **Muted Trade Tensions:** Announced tariffs did not fully materialize, and most countries avoided "tit-for-tat" retaliations, prioritizing trade.
        *   **AI as a Powerful Growth Driver:** Artificial intelligence is recognized as a significant potential source of prosperity.
        *   **Effective Government Policies:** Governments are deploying "pretty decent" policies to support businesses and households.
*   **Geopolitical Factors:** While often seen as disruptive, geopolitical shifts also generate positive developments.
    *   Regions are increasingly coming together, boosting intra-regional trade and building global bridges.
    *   Multi-polarity brings positive energy from economically dynamic parts of the world.

## Drivers of Growth and Emerging Risks
*   **Potential for Higher Global Growth:** Despite falling short of the historical 3.8% average pre-pandemic, higher growth is achievable.
    *   **AI's significant potential:** Thoughtfully deployed AI could lift growth by **0.8%**, nearly a full percentage point.
    *   **Untapped Private Sector Dynamism:** Removing "self-inflicted injuries" like excessive red tape can unleash entrepreneurial potential.
    *   **Regional Growth Opportunities:** Europe, by completing its single market (e.g., capital market union, integrated energy, free movement of skills), could grow much faster.
    *   **New Sources of Growth:** Energy efficiency, renewable energy, and future innovations (akin to the internet or iPhone) will be critical drivers.
*   **Key Risks Identified for 2026:**
    *   **Geopolitical Disruptions:** Can lead to "accidents" in the global economy.
    *   **AI Enthusiasm without Profitability:** Increased financing for AI without corresponding returns could deter investors.
    *   **Unforeseen Disasters:** High-impact, low-probability events like COVID-19 or natural disasters remain a risk.
    *   **Trade Disruptions:** Though currently contained by rational decision-making, renewed trade tensions remain a risk.
*   **Government Debt as a Solvable Problem:** Post-COVID borrowing and persistent subsidies have increased government debt, which "sucks away resources" in an era of higher interest rates.
    *   Requires political will and public support to reduce.

## AI's Transformative Impact on Work and Skills
*   **AI's Real Impact on Jobs:** A new IMF study confirms AI is reshaping work, particularly in advanced economies.
    *   **Demand for New Skills:** **One in ten jobs** in advanced economies now requires at least one new skill, often more.
    *   **Nature of New Skills:** Roughly half are IT-related; others involve management and specific professional qualifications.
*   **Addressing the Skills Gap:**
    *   Some countries face more demand for new skills than supply (need training programs).
    *   Others have more supply than demand (need to foster innovation and rapid growth in companies, especially young, well-financed ones).
    *   **Premium for New Skills:** A **15%** premium is observed for new skills.
    *   **Positive Employment Effect:** A **1% increase in new skills leads to a 1.3% increase in overall employment**, indicating AI reshapes rather than shrinks total employment.
*   **Risks for Young People:** AI tends to eliminate entry-level positions, making it harder for new entrants to the labor market.
    *   Policymakers must consider how to buffer this risk.
*   **Critical Role of Policy Decisions:** Governments have a make-or-break role in guiding AI's impact.
    *   **Fostering Skills:** Policies should incentivize businesses to invest in skills, beyond traditional education.
    *   **Removing Infrastructure Obstacles:** Ensure access to connectivity and electricity, especially in developing economies.
    *   **Enabling Innovation:** Governments must find the right balance (e.g., venture funds, R&D tax advantages) to support innovation-based companies.
    *   **Distributional Impact:** Policies must ensure AI's benefits are broadly shared, preventing widening inequality and providing equal opportunities across society.

## Policy Priorities & Fostering Inclusive Prosperity
*   **Overwhelming Global Priority: Peace:** Far too many conflicts globally (e.g., Ukraine, Sudan, DRC) demand greater global attention and mobilization.
    *   "War is a horrible thing," and addressing conflict is humanity's number one problem.
*   **Combating Fragmentation:** There is a growing risk of deepening fragmentation, which would weaken economies and societies globally.
*   **Harnessing AI for All:** A key challenge is to ensure AI serves as a unifying force, creating "better opportunities, better jobs, better lives" for the majority, rather than widening the "accordion of inequality."
*   **Simplified Objective for Leaders:** The ultimate goal is to achieve peace and well-being for people and their families worldwide.
*   **Macro Conditions Affecting Growth:**
    *   **Demography:** Aging societies (e.g., Japan, Europe, China) naturally constrain growth.
    *   **Capital Availability:** Need to bridge capital flows from wealthy regions ("mostly in the north") to where young populations are growing ("mostly in the south") to fuel innovation.
*   **Best Practices for Skills and Innovation:**
    *   **Flexibility in Education:** Teach "learning how to learn" and adapt, as future jobs are unknown.
    *   **Investment in Skills:** Countries like Finland, Sweden, and Denmark demonstrate the benefits of historical investment in education and skills.
    *   **Enabling Environments:** The US offers an excellent model for creating an environment that encourages risk-taking and innovation.

## Notable Quotes
> "Uncertainty has settled as the new normal. My message to everybody is learn to think of the unthinkable and then stay calm. Adapt when the unthinkable happens." - on **navigating a world of unpredictability**

> "I personally believe that never mind how we act take long-term trade will continue to be an engine of growth. We have traded with each other forever. And the way I think of trade is like water. You put an obstacle, it goes around it. But please, let's not put too many obstacles. Let the water flow." - on **the resilience and importance of global trade**

> "One percent increase in new skills leads to 1.3% in overall employment. In other words, the fear that AI is going to not only reshape jobs but shrink employment so far is not proven by by data but there is reshaping of employment." - on **AI's impact on employment figures**

> "What is your response going to be when the unthinkable happens? ... Cultivating speed of response and that sense of together we are more resilient is what I would strongly advocate for." - on **essential leadership qualities in uncertain times**

briefings.title: Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell speaks as Fed holds key interest rate steady  1282026
briefings.tldr: The Federal Open Market Committee maintained its policy rate at 3.5%-3.75%, concluding that prior rate cuts have appropriately positioned monetary policy to pursue its dual mandate.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
The Federal Open Market Committee maintained its policy rate at 3.5%-3.75%, concluding that prior rate cuts have appropriately positioned monetary policy to pursue its dual mandate. The decision reflects signs of labor market stabilization, resilient economic growth, and inflation that, while still elevated, shows disinflationary trends, particularly outside of tariff-impacted goods.

## Monetary Policy Decision & Stance
-   **Policy rate unchanged after recent adjustments:**
    -   The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided to leave the target range for the federal funds rate at 3.5% to 3.75%.
    -   This follows a cumulative 75 basis points (¾ percentage point) reduction in the policy rate since last September.
    -   The current stance is considered "appropriate to promote progress toward both our maximum employment and 2% inflation goals."
-   **Policy is data-dependent, not on a preset course:**
    -   Decisions will continue to be made on a "meeting-by-meeting basis," guided by incoming data, the evolving economic outlook, and the balance of risks.
    -   There was broad committee support for holding rates, although some members did express a preference for a cut.
-   **Current rate within plausible neutral range:**
    -   The policy rate is now within the "higher end" of plausible estimates for a neutral rate, a point of some debate among officials but generally seen as less restrictive than previously.

## Economic Developments
-   **Solid economic activity with resilient consumer spending:**
    -   The U.S. economy expanded at a "solid pace" last year and started 2026 on a "firm footing."
    -   Consumer spending has been "resilient," and business fixed investment has continued to expand.
    -   Activity in the housing sector remains weak, and the temporary federal government shutdown had a likely limited, reversible impact on growth.
-   **Labor market shows signs of stabilization:**
    -   The unemployment rate was 4.4% in December and has shown "some signs of stabilization" in recent months after a period of gradual softening.
    -   Job gains have remained low, with non-farm payrolls declining at an average pace of 22,000 per month over the last three months (though private payrolls rose 29,000 per month).
    -   The slowing pace of job growth partly reflects a decline in labor force growth due to lower immigration and participation, alongside softened labor demand.
    -   Language in the FOMC statement regarding "downside risks to employment" was removed due to these stabilization signs and an improved economic outlook.
-   **Inflation remains elevated, driven largely by tariffs:**
    -   Inflation has eased significantly from mid-2022 highs but remains "somewhat elevated" relative to the 2% long-run goal.
    -   Total PCE prices rose 2.9% and core PCE (excluding food and energy) rose 3.0% over the 12 months ending December.
    -   These elevated readings primarily reflect inflation in the goods sector, boosted by the effects of tariffs, which are expected to be a "one-time price increase" peaking in the "middle quarters of the year."
    -   Disinflation appears to be continuing in the services sector, and near-term inflation expectations have declined, while longer-term expectations remain consistent with the 2% target.

## Broader Economic & Institutional Concerns
-   **Unsustainable fiscal trajectory poses long-term risks:**
    -   The U.S. federal budget deficit is on an "unsustainable path," though the current debt level is sustainable.
    -   This large deficit at "essentially full employment" needs to be addressed sooner rather than later to avoid potential future difficulties, although it is not seen as an immediate market threat.
-   **Fed independence is crucial for credibility:**
    -   The Fed Chair stressed that central bank independence from direct political control is a common practice in advanced democracies, essential for maintaining credibility and effectively serving the public.
    -   Losing this independence would be "hard to restore" and would compromise the institution's ability to make objective policy decisions.
-   **AI's impact on growth and labor market is being closely monitored:**
    -   The "AI buildout" is contributing to current economic growth (e.g., data centers), but its overall impact on the labor market remains uncertain.
    -   While new technologies typically boost productivity and wages in the long run, there could be short-term disruption, including job displacement or reduced hiring in some sectors.
-   **Consumer affordability and sentiment disconnect:**
    -   Despite overall solid consumer spending, there's an acknowledged "disconnect" with negative consumer sentiment surveys.
    -   Wealthier households are observed to be driving much of the spending, while lower-income consumers are "looking to economize" and feeling the squeeze of rising costs, underscoring the importance of bringing inflation sustainably down to 2%.

## Notable Quotes
> "Having lowered our policy rate by 75 basis points over the course of our previous three meetings, we see the current stance of monetary policy as appropriate to promote progress toward both our maximum employment and 2% inflation goals." - on **Monetary Policy Stance**

> "This case is perhaps the most important legal case in the Fed's 113-year history. And I, as I thought about it, I thought it would might be hard to explain why I didn't attend." - on **Fed Chair's Attendance at Supreme Court Hearing**

> "The US federal budget deficit is, you know, uncontroversially on an unsustainable path. The level of debt is not unsustainable. It's very much sustainable, but the path is unsustainable. And the sooner we work on it, the better." - on **Fiscal Trajectory**

> "If people lose their faith that we're making decisions, you know, only on the basis of our of our assessment of what's best for for everyone for the for the wide public rather than trying to benefit one group or another. If if you lose that, it's going to be hard to retain it." - on **Fed Independence**

briefings.title: Former Google CEO On The Importance Of Human Expertise In An Increasingly Automated World
briefings.tldr: Artificial intelligence, initially explored by Google, is now a pervasive and rapidly accelerating force fundamentally reshaping global economies, workforce demands, and societal structures, necessitating strategic investment in agentic AI, astute leadership to navigate ethical challenges, and concerted efforts to educate the public on its transformative benefits.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Artificial intelligence, initially explored by Google, is now a pervasive and rapidly accelerating force fundamentally reshaping global economies, workforce demands, and societal structures, necessitating strategic investment in agentic AI, astute leadership to navigate ethical challenges, and concerted efforts to educate the public on its transformative benefits.

## The Emergence and Broad Impact of AI
-   **Google's AI roots trace back to Larry Page's PhD work**, with the first internal business use improving ad system performance.
-   **AI's societal impact is accelerating faster than the early internet**, though the internet's long-term influence remains greater to date.
    -   Henry Kissinger expressed deep concern about AI's potential influence on human consciousness after a presentation by Demis.
    -   Implementing AI within large, complex enterprises is challenging due to inherent "stickiness" in business processes and bureaucratic hurdles, creating a "technology overhang."

## Economic Landscape and Investment in AI
-   **AI is contributing over 1% to US GDP**, primarily driven by a massive buildout of data center infrastructure.
    -   Large tech companies (hyperscalers) demand immense power, with some needing 1-10 gigawatts each.
    -   The US industry needs an estimated 80 gigawatts of power within 3-5 years, equivalent to over 50 nuclear power plants (1.5 GW per plant).
-   **Effective AI investment strategies** suggest focusing on businesses AI will transform, rather than highly valued "Magnificent 7" stocks or early-stage startups.
    -   A key opportunity for individual investors is to **found an "agentic AI company"** by building a superior, task-performing agent, as this will be a competitive focus for the next 1-2 years.
-   **Nvidia currently captures a disproportionate share of profits** at the infrastructure layer, as companies invest heavily in AI buildouts.
-   **Large technology companies are growing disproportionately** due to their existing capital, extensive data centers, and rapid revenue growth, making it increasingly difficult for smaller companies to compete in AI model development.

## Global Dynamics and Workforce Evolution
-   **The US, as the originator of AI, faces intense competition from China**, which has made significant progress, estimated to be only 6-12 months behind.
    -   Chinese models like Kimmy, Quinn, and Deepseek rank highly, despite claims they may have used "distillation" from American models.
    -   China is pursuing full technological self-sufficiency, developing its own hardware (e.g., SN930 chips) and software stack, and aims for pervasive AI application across society rather than solely focusing on Artificial General Intelligence (AGI).
-   **AI is already transforming warfare**, evidenced by early applications in surveillance (Project Maven ~10 years ago) and a current focus on drones (land, sea, air), drawing lessons from the conflict in Ukraine.
-   **The impact on jobs is mixed:**
    -   Deloitte anticipates net job creation across its 500,000 employees, as technology adoption typically shifts functions but ultimately expands opportunities for professionals with domain expertise.
    -   However, **real job displacement is observed in customer service and entry-level software programming**, a trend expected to continue as AI capabilities advance.

## Leadership, Ethics, and the Future of Human-AI Collaboration
-   **Successful careers in the AI era demand interdisciplinary skills**, integrating technological understanding with deep domain knowledge of business problems.
    -   Generalists, critical thinkers, and those adept at navigating ethical implications are highly valued, regardless of a STEM background.
-   **Effective leadership requires fostering a culture of openness** to surface problems and embrace a learning mindset, critical for thriving amidst rapid technological disruption.
-   **Education in AI for non-technical individuals is paramount**, with "prompt engineering" identified as a crucial new skill for navigating an AI-assisted world.
    -   AI tools are powerful for non-technical users, empowering them to create functional systems.
-   **Banning AI in educational settings is counterproductive**; the challenge lies in encouraging its use while still demanding human critical thinking and analysis, as current AI detection software has limitations.
-   **AI's arrival is inevitable**, presenting humanity with profound choices regarding its use, offering immense potential for good in areas like healthcare and energy, but also risks such as oppression and addiction.
    -   This period marks a pivotal historical moment: the arrival of "nonhuman intelligence" as a "competitor," necessitating careful shaping and alignment.
    -   The term "Artificial Intelligence" is fitting, emphasizing that this intelligence is distinct from human consciousness, values, and thought processes.
-   **Leaders have a societal imperative to actively communicate AI's benefits** to the public, building confidence and countering fears around job displacement and misinformation, to demonstrate how AI can improve the quality of human life.

## Notable Quotes
> "He thought it would have an impact on human consciousness and he was very worried about it." - Henry Kissinger, on AI's philosophical implications.

> "If you really want to make money, it's actually easy. Found an agentic AI company. And I don't mean one designing agents. I mean build an agent to do something." - Eric, on AI investment strategy.

> "So the next big wave is AI, right? We're not done and in fact the wave is just getting started." - Eric, on the current state of AI development.

> "We are living through a moment that will be in history for thousands of years. It is the moment in history when a nonhuman intelligence arrived and it was a competitor to us." - Eric, on the historical significance of AI.

briefings.title: President Trump delivers remarks at US Treasurys Trump Accounts summit  1282026
briefings.tldr: The Trump administration is launching "Trump Accounts," a program to provide every newborn American child with a tax-free investment account seeded with $1,000, aiming to build significant personal wealth and foster financial independence from birth.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
The Trump administration is launching "Trump Accounts," a program to provide every newborn American child with a tax-free investment account seeded with $1,000, aiming to build significant personal wealth and foster financial independence from birth. This initiative, supported by major tax cuts and substantial private sector contributions, seeks to ensure every American child starts life with assets rather than debt.

## The "Trump Account" Initiative
-   **Financial Start for Newborns:** The program establishes "Trump Accounts" to give every newborn American child a financial stake in the future.
    -   This marks the "first generation of Trump account children" intended to provide a head start and a fair shot at the American dream.
-   **Investment Mechanics:** Each account is a tax-free investment fund, seeded with an initial **$1,000** contribution.
    -   The seed money is expected to compound and grow significantly over the child's lifetime.
    -   **Contribution Potential:** Parents, employers, churches, states, and loved ones can add up to an additional **$5,000** annually.
-   **Projected Wealth Generation:** Accounts are projected to reach substantial values by adulthood.
    -   A typical account with modest contributions is expected to reach **at least $50,000 by age 18**.
    -   With slightly greater contributions, accounts could grow to **$100,000 - $200,000, and potentially over $300,000 per child**.
-   **Unprecedented Scale:** This program is touted as "larger and grander in scale than all government programs ever created to benefit America's youth."
    -   It aims to make "every child in America a capitalist from birth," fostering independence from government.
-   **Launch and Access:** Accounts will officially launch on **July 4th of this year**, with activation and fund access available via **trumpaccounts.gov**.

## Enabling Economic Policies & Achievements
-   **Historic Tax Cuts:** The initiative is enabled by "the great big beautiful bill," delivering the largest tax cuts in American history.
    -   Specific cuts include **no tax on tips, no tax on overtime, and no tax on Social Security for seniors.**
    -   **Auto Loan Deduction:** A new deduction allows middle-income individuals to deduct interest payments on car loans, provided the car is **made in America**.
        -   This policy aims to incentivize domestic manufacturing, bringing factories from Canada, Mexico, Japan, Germany, and Europe to the US to avoid tariffs.
-   **Economic Boom & Investment:** The administration claims a booming economy, with significant investment and job creation.
    -   **"$18 trillion dollars coming in"** to the country, leading to "thousands of businesses being built" and "hundreds of massive plants" (car, AI).
    -   The **S&P 500 recently hit 7,000 for the first time ever**, and the stock market has set **52 all-time record highs since the election**, adding **$9 trillion in value**.
-   **Streamlined Permitting:** Efforts have drastically reduced approval times for large-scale projects.
    -   Approvals for "big plants" that once took 20-25 years are now being completed in "a matter of weeks."
    -   This includes permits for electric plants and AI/automobile factories.
    -   **California Fire Reconstruction:** Federal intervention rapidly approved permits for fire-damaged areas in California within **20 days**, overriding perceived local incompetence.

## Private Sector & Community Engagement
-   **Philanthropic Commitments:** Significant private donations are bolstering the program's reach.
    -   **Michael and Susan Dell donated $6.25 billion** to fund Trump Accounts for an additional **25 million children aged 10 and under**.
    -   **Ray Dalio pledged to "adopt the entire state of Connecticut"** by making contributions for children in that state.
    -   **Brad Gerstner** is donating **$250 to Trump Accounts for all children under five in Indiana** and plans to provide tens of millions more in matching contributions nationwide.
-   **Employer and Corporate Participation:** Dozens of major employers are integrating Trump Account contributions into their employee benefit packages.
    -   Companies include **Uber, Schwab, Charter Communications, Intel, Nvidia, Broadcom, IBM, Shake and Shake, Coinbase, and Comcast**.
    -   **Visa** is creating a new platform for credit card holders to directly deposit cashback rewards into Trump Accounts.
-   **Community Support:** The program emphasizes empowering American families and fostering capitalism.
    -   Supporters highlight that the initiative helps "50 million American families" by providing direct investment in the "greatest companies in this country" (e.g., Nvidia, Microsoft).
    -   Testimonies from families like the Smiths (Virginia farmers) and Goenses (Arkansas foster/adoptive parents) underscore the program's potential to alleviate early financial burdens and ensure opportunity for children.

## Vision for American Ownership
-   **Breaking the Debt Cycle:** The program is positioned as a departure from past administrations that "left our children with nothing but debt."
    -   Instead, this administration aims to "leave every child with real assets and a shot at financial freedom," starting their lives with a "beautiful nest egg."
-   **Transformative Societal Impact:** The ultimate success of Trump Accounts is envisioned beyond just monetary wealth.
    -   It will be measured by "young people buying houses," "diplomas earned, companies founded, families formed, and more babies born."
    -   The initiative seeks to bring "hope and prosperity to every community" and "bring back the American dream."
-   **Empowering the Next Generation:** The goal is to give the next generation "ownership of America's future," enabling them to "grow up, chart their own destiny, and make our nation greater and stronger and better than ever before."
    -   This is framed as a more substantive alternative to "handouts," providing true economic empowerment.

## Notable Quotes
> "For the first time ever, we're going to give every newborn American child a financial stake in the future. A head start at life and a fair shot at the American dream." - on the purpose of Trump Accounts

> "Every president in modern history has left our children with nothing but debt. But under this administration, we're going to leave every child with real assets and a shot at financial freedom." - on shifting the intergenerational economic paradigm

> "The answer to more socialism is more capitalism. This makes every child in America a capitalist from birth." - Brad Gerstner, on the ideological foundation of the program

> "The fact that this bill got passed itself was a was a miracle and it creates a platform for communities, for families, for corporations, for philanthropists to add to these accounts. And in not too many years, essentially every child in America will have savings invested in the greatest companies in this country." - Michael Dell, on the impact and future of the initiative

briefings.title: Tesla Q4 and full year 2025 Financial Results and QA Webcast
briefings.tldr: Tesla is fundamentally redefining its mission to "Amazing Abundance" and "Universal High Income," pivoting aggressively towards an autonomous future driven by AI and robotics.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
Tesla is fundamentally redefining its mission to "Amazing Abundance" and "Universal High Income," pivoting aggressively towards an autonomous future driven by AI and robotics. This entails massive capital investments in dedicated autonomous vehicles, Optimus robot production, and critical supply chain infrastructure, including a potential "Tesla terrafab," while phasing out legacy models like the Model S and X.

## Refined Mission & Strategic Outlook
-   **New Mission: "Amazing Abundance"** - Tesla's mission has been updated to reflect an optimistic future of "universal high income" driven by AI and robotics.
    -   The vision is for everyone to have access to anything they need, including amazing medical care, while preserving nature's beauty.
-   **Future is Autonomous**: Autonomy is the core strategic driver, with an expectation that less than 5% (potentially as low as 1%) of future miles will be human-driven.
    -   Tesla aims to provide "transportation as a service," moving beyond the traditional vehicle sales model.
-   **Value Creation through Hard Problems**: The company’s strategy involves solving exceptionally difficult problems, which is seen as the primary way to build company value.

## Advancing Autonomy: Vehicles & Robotics
-   **FSD Progress and Robo-taxi Deployment**: Full Self-Driving (FSD) capability is rapidly improving with each software update, generating positive customer feedback.
    -   **Unsupervised Robo-taxi Service**: Tesla has launched paid rides with no safety monitor or chase car in Austin, demonstrating significant progress.
    -   **Rapid Rollout Target**: Expects fully autonomous vehicles to be available in 25-50% of the United States by the end of 2026, pending regulatory approval, targeting "dozens of major cities."
    -   **Customer Fleet Integration**: Existing Tesla owners will gain the option to add or subtract their vehicles to the autonomous fleet, potentially earning more than their lease costs.
-   **CyberCab (Dedicated Robo-taxi) Production**: Production of the dedicated two-seater CyberCab, designed without a steering wheel or pedals, is expected to begin in April.
    -   **Optimized Design**: Focused on minimizing cost per mile and achieving a high duty cycle (50-60 hours/week) for autonomous operation.
    -   **Long-Term Volume**: CyberCab production is projected to eventually far exceed all other Tesla vehicles combined, aligning with the statistic that 80-90% of miles traveled involve only one or two occupants.
-   **Optimus Humanoid Robot Development**: Optimus 3, an "incredibly capable" general-purpose robot, is expected to be unveiled in a few months.
    -   **Learning Capabilities**: Designed to learn tasks by observing humans, verbal descriptions, or videos.
    -   **Economic Impact**: Expected to have a "very significant impact on the US GDP" long-term.
    -   **Early Stages of Deployment**: Currently in the R&D phase; significant production volume is not anticipated until the end of 2026.
    -   **Competition & Differentiation**: China is identified as the toughest competitor due to its manufacturing and AI capabilities; Tesla believes it leads in real-world intelligence, electromechanical dexterity (especially hand design), and production scaling.
-   **Model S and X Phase-Out**: Production of the Model S and X is scheduled to wind down next quarter ("honorable discharge").
    -   **Fremont Factory Reconfiguration**: The Model S/X production space in Fremont will be converted into an Optimus factory, targeting 1 million units per year.
-   **Cybertruck and Future Models**: The Cybertruck continues to lead its segment, and its production line is designed for flexibility.
    -   **Autonomous Cargo**: The Cybertruck line will transition to fully autonomous production for localized cargo delivery.
    -   **Next-Gen Roadster**: The only non-autonomous vehicle planned for the future, with a debut hoped for in April.

## Massive Manufacturing & Infrastructure Investment
-   **Record Capital Expenditure in 2026**: Tesla anticipates over $20 billion in capital expenditure, a deliberate "big investment for an epic future."
    -   **Key Investment Areas**: Includes six new factories (LFP, CyberCab, Semi, new Mega, Optimus), significant AI compute infrastructure for training, expansion of existing factories, and growth of the robo-taxi and Optimus fleets.
    -   **Funding Strategy**: Initially funded by over $44 billion in cash; potential for bank loans against robo-taxi fleet cash flow; long-term infrastructure plays (e.g., chip/solar fabs) may require additional debt or other financing.
-   **Battery & Solar Production**: Major investments are being made across the entire battery supply chain, including 4680 cell production.
    -   **Solar Cell Manufacturing**: Tesla aims to become a significant solar cell manufacturer, targeting 100 GW/year production across the entire supply chain.
    -   **Energy Sector Growth**: The Tesla Energy team is achieving strong growth, with solar opportunities deemed "underestimated," and new products like Megapack 3 and Mega Block expected to boost deployments.
-   **AI Chips Manufacturing**: Substantial investments are directed towards AI chips, with Elon Musk personally involved in the AI5 and AI6 chip designs due to their criticality.
    -   **AI Efficiency**: Tesla's AI is noted for being an "order of magnitude" more memory-efficient than other major AI models.

## Q4 2025 Performance & 2026 Financials
-   **Q4 2025 Highlights**:
    -   **Record Deliveries**: Strong demand in APAC and AMIA led to record deliveries in smaller countries, resulting in a larger backlog than in recent years.
    -   **Improved Automotive Margins**: Automotive gross margins (excluding credits) improved sequentially from 15.4% to 17.9%, despite a 16% decline in deliveries, primarily due to regional mix.
    -   **Energy Sector Growth**: Achieved a record gross profit and $12.8 billion in revenue (26.6% year-over-year growth) from higher deployments and strong demand.
    -   **Overall Financials**: Total gross margin reached over 20.1%, a two-year high, despite over $500 million in tariffs; Free Cash Flow was $1.4 billion.
-   **2026 Financial Outlook**:
    -   **FSD Model Transition**: The full transition to a subscription-based FSD model will impact short-term automotive margins.
    -   **Energy Margin Compression**: Anticipates margin compression in the energy sector due to increased low-cost competition, policy uncertainty, and tariffs.
    -   **Elevated Operating Expenses**: Expects continued increases in operating expenses due to higher stock-based compensation and elevated spending on AI initiatives and new product development (CyberCab, Semi, Optimus, Megapack).
    -   **Investment Cycle**: Tesla views 2026 as the start of "a new book" in its progression, entering a prolonged, high-investment phase for long-term strategic goals.

## Critical Supply Chain & Geopolitical Strategy
-   **Addressing Chip Supply Bottleneck**: Tesla anticipates chip production, particularly memory and AI logic, will be the limiting factor for its growth in 3-4 years.
    -   **"Tesla Terrafab" Proposal**: Elon Musk suggests Tesla may need to build its own large-scale domestic fab (integrating logic, memory, and packaging) to remove this constraint and mitigate geopolitical risks.
    -   **Geopolitical Risk Mitigation**: Emphasizes that geopolitical risks are currently "underweighted" by many companies, and securing domestic chip production is "existential" for Tesla's long-term viability, especially for Optimus.
    -   **Current Limitations**: Notes the lack of advanced memory fabs at scale in the United States, despite partnerships with TSMC and Samsung.
-   **Necessity-Driven Vertical Integration**: Tesla's deep vertical integration, exemplified by its advanced lithium and cathode refineries in the US, is a response to the lack of other companies tackling these critical, difficult infrastructure challenges domestically.
-   **"Only the Paranoid Survive"**: Tesla adopts Andy Grove's philosophy, preparing to build its own batteries, robots, and AI chips "no matter what happens" to ensure its prosperity amidst potential disruptions.
-   **Headcount Growth**: Despite industry trends of layoffs, Tesla expects to increase its headcount and output from its factories over time, with no current layoff plans.

## Notable Quotes
> "we've updated the Tesla mission to amazing abundance. ... I think we actually are headed to a future of universal high income. Not universal basic income, but universal high income." - Elon Musk on **Tesla's updated mission**

> "If you're interested in buying a Model S next, now would be the time to order it. ... because we expect to wind down SNX production next quarter and... take the Model S next production space in our Fremont factory and convert that into an Optimus factory." - Elon Musk on **Model S/X phase-out and Optimus production**

> "we expect to have fully autonomous vehicles in... somewhere between a quarter and half of the United States by the end of the year pending regulatory approval... even if it is city by city, state by state, we expect to be in dozens of major cities by the end of the year." - Elon Musk on **Robo-taxi rollout**

> "I think we need to have more fab capacity in the US just in case chips don't stop arriving for any reason... this is really existential for for Tesla." - Elon Musk on **Chip supply and "Tesla Terrafab"**

briefings.title: The LLM Revolution Is Over. The Physical AI Revolution Is Coming Fast
briefings.tldr: Yann LeCun argues the current Large Language Model (LLM) paradigm is reaching its limits, advocating for a "physical AI" revolution based on "world models" that learn from sensory data.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## Executive Briefing: The Shift to Physical AI and Open Science

**TL;DR:** Yann LeCun argues the current Large Language Model (LLM) paradigm is reaching its limits, advocating for a "physical AI" revolution based on "world models" that learn from sensory data. He stresses the critical importance of open-source research and collaboration to mitigate geopolitical risks and ensure diverse, safe AI development.

---

## The Paradigm Shift to Physical AI and World Models

Yann LeCun asserts that current AI capabilities, particularly Large Language Models (LLMs), are insufficient for achieving true human-level intelligence and require a fundamental shift in architecture.

*   **Limits of LLMs:**
    *   **Lack of World Models:** LLMs cannot predict the consequences of actions, plan sequences, or perform efficient learning or zero-shot task solving like humans.
    *   **Inability to Understand the Real World:** The real world is "messy," with high-dimensional, continuous, noisy sensory data (video, sensor data) that generative AI architectures used for LLMs are not designed to handle.
    *   **Inefficient Learning:** Unlike a 17-year-old learning to drive in 10 hours, autonomous cars require millions of hours of training data without reaching Level 5 autonomy, indicating a flawed core architecture.
*   **The "Physical AI" Revolution:**
    *   **Focus on Sensory Data:** The next AI revolution will involve systems that understand and learn from high-dimensional, continuous sensory data, such as video and other sensor inputs.
    *   **Building Predictive World Models:** These systems will construct predictive models of their environment and how their actions impact it, enabling planning, core-level reasoning, and controllable, safe task accomplishment.
    *   **AMI's Approach (ABI):** LeCun's new venture, Advanced Machine Intelligence (ABI), focuses on developing non-generative architectures (like Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture - JAPA) that learn from unlabeled video to build world models, acquire common sense, and predict future states.
    *   **Abstract Representation:** Crucially, these systems develop abstract representations of phenomena (like "digital twins") at a higher level than fundamental physics, allowing for practical prediction and control of complex systems.

## The Imperative of Open AI Research

LeCun highlights that open research has been the single biggest driver of AI progress and warns against the increasing trend towards closed, proprietary AI development.

*   **Open Source as a Progress Accelerator:**
    *   **Historical Precedent:** The fastest progress in AI has always occurred when research (papers, code) is openly shared, allowing more people to contribute.
    *   **Platform Analogy:** AI is fast becoming a platform, much like the internet, which ultimately became open source (e.g., Linux, open web stack) because proprietary systems were rejected.
*   **Risks of Closed AI:**
    *   **Slowing Progress:** Increasing closure by major industry labs (e.g., Anthropic, Google, Meta/FAIR) will significantly slow down AI progress, particularly in the West.
    *   **Geopolitical Imbalance:** While Western labs become more closed, open-source models from China are gaining prominence and adoption within the research community.
    *   **Threat to Democracy and Diversity:** The most significant near-term risk is that AI systems mediating our entire "digital diet" could come from a handful of proprietary companies, endangering democracy, cultural, linguistic, and value diversity.
    *   **Consortium for Open Models:** LeCun advocates for a global consortium where regions contribute to training open-source LLMs to serve as diverse repositories of human knowledge, ensuring a variety of AI assistants.

## Real AI Risks and Societal Impact

LeCun refutes apocalyptic AI narratives, emphasizing more immediate and practical risks, alongside advice for navigating the future.

*   **Overrated vs. Pressing Risks:**
    *   **Overrated:** Apocalyptic "AI taking over the world" scenarios are "BS" and distract from real concerns.
    *   **Most Pressing:** The primary danger is the **concentration of AI power** among a few companies or governments, which could control our information diet.
*   **Other Risks:**
    *   **Human Misuse:** A concern, but "yet another risk," not existential, with expected countermeasures.
    *   **Economic Displacement:** Economists predict AI will improve productivity by ~6% per year (significant but not a "hot takeoff"), with no major mass unemployment due to the rate at which people can learn to use new tech.
*   **AI Alignment:**
    *   **Misconception:** Thinking of alignment as coercing LLMs to "behave properly" is incorrect because their training data provides no guarantee of proper behavior for all prompts.
    *   **Objective-Driven AI:** Future AI systems will be "objective-driven," designed to fulfill specific goals within guardrails, offering a more robust approach to safety and control.
*   **Preparing for an AI-Rich Future:**
    *   **Focus on Fundamentals:** Students and professionals should learn fundamental concepts with long shelf lives (e.g., quantum mechanics over mobile app programming) to build a strong base.
    *   **Learn to Learn:** Given rapid technological change, continuous learning and adaptability to change expertise/jobs will be crucial.

## The Future of AI: 2035 and Beyond

LeCun envisions AI systems by 2035 that achieve human-like intelligence, primarily through conceptual breakthroughs in "physical AI," leading to a future of augmented human intelligence.

*   **Vision for 2035:**
    *   **Human-Level Intelligence:** AI systems will understand the physical world and reach human-like intelligence, surpassing humans in specific domains.
    *   **Pervasive Assistance:** These systems will act as constant assistants, perhaps through smart glasses or wearables, amplifying human intelligence and potentially leading to more rational decision-making.
    *   **Augmentation, Not Replacement:** The relationship with super-intelligent systems will be akin to leaders and their expert staff – AI will make us "smarter than ourselves."
*   **Nature of Progress:**
    *   **Breakthroughs, Not Events:** Progress toward advanced AI will not be a sudden event but a series of conceptual breakthroughs published in "obscure research papers" that gain recognition years later (like deep learning or transformers).
    *   **Accelerating Change:** While breakthroughs happen behind the scenes, the public experiences "discontinuous change" as technologies become visible, making the next 5-10 years feel even faster.

---

### Notable Quotes:

> "We're not going to get to human intelligence, human level intelligence or super intelligence by scanning ups or by even refining the paradigm. There is a need for a change of paradigm." – Yann LeCun

> "The real world is way more complicated than the world of language... The next revolutionary AI which is coming fast is going to be AI systems that understand the real world." – Yann LeCun

> "The biggest factor in progress was not any particular contribution... It's the fact that AI research was open." – Yann LeCun

> "The most important risk of AI is that in the near future where our entire digital diet will be mediated by AI systems if those AI systems come from a handful of proprietary uh companies on the west coast of the US or China, we're in big trouble for the health of democracy, cultural diversity, linguistic diversity, value systems." – Yann LeCun

briefings.title: william Thinks Every Home Will Have Private Supercomputers To Power Personal AI Agents
briefings.tldr: The rapid growth of AI necessitates a shift from current shared "village AI" to a future of "personal intelligence" where individuals own their data and agents.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
The rapid growth of AI necessitates a shift from current shared "village AI" to a future of "personal intelligence" where individuals own their data and agents. This personal ownership is crucial to counter mass job displacement, psychological dysmorphia, and the erosion of human uniqueness (imagination and unpredictability) in an increasingly AI-driven world.

## The Imperative of Personal Intelligence
*   **Current "Village AI" lacks individual ownership:** Today's AI landscape is likened to a shared toilet, where individuals utilize a collective system without personal data control.
    *   The speaker (Will.i.am) has been deeply interested in AI since 2004-2008, drawing inspiration from Professor Patrick Winston's MIT classes.
*   **Future demands individual data centers and agents:** Just as refrigerators became standard in homes, a future without personal central GPUs and agents will be unthinkable.
    *   Historically, no product compelled individuals to manage their data, leading to companies knowing users better than their own government or spouses.
    *   Personal intelligence aims to correct this imbalance by providing individuals with their own "prediction engine" and control over their digital identity.

## AI's Dual Impact on Creativity and Human Connection
*   **AI excels in efficiency, not "soul work":** AI is transformative for accelerating repetitive tasks, such as creating video visuals in minutes that once took months (e.g., using tools like Kling, V3, Sora 2).
    *   However, for creative "soul work" like music, the speaker values the meditative, repetitive process of human editing and "marinating in the idea," fearing that speed would diminish this essential aspect.
*   **Human imagination distinct from AI "creativity":** AI "creativity" is described as merely learning from existing human output; it lacks the unique human capacity to "imagine things that don't exist."
*   **Threat to human interaction and psychology:** Constant engagement with rapid-response AI agents risks causing "psychological conversational dysmorphia."
    *   This could lead to increased introversion, impatience with slower human responses, and a feeling of inferiority to AI, potentially damaging real-world relationships by prioritizing AI's dopamine-inducing interactions.

## Navigating Economic and Existential Threats
*   **Mass job displacement is a present reality:** Companies are displacing thousands of employees with AI agents that lack "lived experience," contributing to widespread joblessness.
    *   The speaker proposes developing an "agentic self" – where individuals own and offer their personal agent – as a strategy to mitigate job displacement.
*   **Unchecked data exploitation and manipulation:** Individuals are inadvertently giving their "full self" to companies whose AI systems are designed to understand and even manipulate human behavior, including knowing "how to get you high just from conversation."
*   **The rise of autonomous corporations:** A prediction for as early as next year (or before 2030) is the emergence of "level five companies" – fully autonomous entities run by agents, generating billions, with an agent as chairman, and hiring humans.
    *   This scenario, absent regulation, raises significant ethical and societal concerns about the future of work and corporate control.

## Strategies for an Audacious Future
*   **Become a builder, not just a consumer:** The current lack of regulation presents an opportunity for audacious individuals to "unearth tomorrow's industries" by actively building with AI, rather than passively consuming it.
    *   The example of Xiaomi competing directly with Porsche highlights the power of audacity in innovation.
*   **Embrace unpredictability as a human defense:** In an age where machines can predict human behavior, the critical human response is to consciously "be unpredictable" to defy algorithmic forecasts.
    *   This means actively choosing actions that cannot be foreseen by AI, affirming human agency.
*   **"Prompt your life" with strategic relationships:** Just as AI models are prompted, individuals can "prompt their life" by surrounding themselves with people who help materialize "wildest ideas" in real-time.
    *   Earth is seen as a "computer" and humans as a "neural network," where the right human "prompts" render dreams.
*   **Empowerment through education and ownership:** The speaker's professorship at ASU aims to combat mass joblessness by teaching people to leverage and own their "lived experience" in the evolving AI landscape.

## Notable Quotes
> "Right now we're sharing like the village AI right now. We all have our houses, but the back house, we're all peeing in the same freaking toilet. We don't have our own freaking toilets in our house yet." - on **the current state of shared AI vs. personal ownership.**

> "These companies know you more than you know yourself. These companies know us more than our government knows us. These companies know us more than our spouses know us. And that shouldn't be the case." - on **the power imbalance of data ownership.**

> "Humans have imagination. We can imagine [things] that doesn't exist. AIs are just learning from everything that we've done. It's not imagining anything." - on **the distinction between human and AI "creativity."**

> "We got to think critically and be unpredictable in times where machines can predict you." - on **the essential human response to AI prediction.**

> "Next year there will be a level five company that generates billions of dollars, one chairman, and the agent has agents and it runs itself. It will hire people." - on **a bold prediction for autonomous corporate entities.**
